findings.title: MFA reset leaves existing application web sessions authorized
findings.scenario: An attacker holds a previously stepped-up Spring web session. An administrator resets the victim's MFA, removing OTP credentials and ending Keycloak sessions. The attacker continues calling protected APIs with the existing application cookie under REQUIRED.
findings.expected: Recovery invalidates application sessions and their old assurance, forcing fresh authentication and enrolment.
findings.actual: Reset only calls Keycloak logout. Spring sessions are neither deleted nor checked against a revocation generation. WebAccountFilter reuses stored OIDC claims, and REQUIRED accepts their old MFA assertion without checking token expiry or reset time. Activity can keep the application session alive beyond the documented access-token lifetime.
findings.evidence: MfaAdminController.java:97-107 removes credentials, logs out at Keycloak and returns sessionsEnded=true. WebAccountFilter.java:31-35 maps user.getClaims() from the stored login on each request. MfaEnforcementFilter.java:42-44 checks only policy and assertsMfa. No application-session invalidation or back-channel logout integration was found.
findings.suggested_fix: Invalidate all affected Spring sessions on reset and disabling, or enforce a server-side authentication generation on every request. Integrate provider logout/revocation events where applicable and report session termination accurately.
findings.repro_test: Runtime test proposed, not executed: establish an MFA web session, reset that account from another administrator, then reuse its cookie against /api/v1/me/addresses under REQUIRED. Require rejection immediately and after the original ID token expires.

findings.title: DISABLED blocks preference enablement but not MFA enrolment or use
findings.scenario: All categories applicable to a user are DISABLED. The user directly visits /oauth2/authorization/keycloak?stepUp=true instead of using the hidden UI controls.
findings.expected: D18 DISABLED makes enrolment and MFA use unavailable while preserving existing factors and independent required controls.
findings.actual: Only preference enablement checks availability. The authorization resolver unconditionally requests MFA for stepUp=true, and the shared Keycloak flow runs OTP or enrolment without consulting category policy. Security settings also return the step-up and account-console URLs while disabled.
findings.evidence: MfaController.java:71-75 always returns both URLs; :94-97 restricts only preference enablement. SecurityConfiguration.java stepUpResolver checks only the stepUp parameter. infra/identity/matbakhy-realm.json:269-283 makes level-2 OTP REQUIRED with no application-policy condition; the enrolment test documents the no-factor path.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce availability in supported provider enrolment/use flows as well as application entry points, while retaining separate mandatory assurance for privileged operations. Do not rely on hiding UI controls.
findings.repro_test: Runtime test proposed, not executed: set all applicable policies DISABLED, invoke the direct step-up URL with a synthetic account lacking OTP, and attempt enrolment. Repeat with an enrolled account and direct account-console access.

findings.title: Partial reset failures can remove factors without a durable reset audit
findings.scenario: Credential deletion succeeds, then another deletion or Keycloak logout fails. Alternatively, the final audit write fails after provider changes have completed.
findings.expected: Every destructive recovery attempt durably records actor, target, reason, completed changes and session-termination outcome, including partial failures.
findings.actual: The only success audit occurs after all remote operations. There is no attempt record or failure handler. A dependency exception can therefore leave OTP removed with no reset audit, and potentially leave provider sessions active.
findings.evidence: MfaAdminController.java:97-101 performs irreversible remote operations before audit.record at :105-106. KeycloakAdmin.deleteCredential/logout throw on unsuccessful responses. The shared denial audit handles AccessDeniedException, not these dependency failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist a reset attempt before destructive calls, then record completion or partial failure with removed-factor count and logout outcome. Use a durable retry/reconciliation mechanism for incomplete session termination.
findings.repro_test: Fault-injection test proposed, not executed: allow credential deletion, fail logout, and verify a durable partial-failure audit with actor, target and reason. Also simulate failure of the final audit write.
